messages:
jamie: quick sync — dropping a lightweight proposal for 'elastic reserved pools' + soft quota tokens. want product + eng alignment before i put this in the roadmap doc.
kevin: thanks. high level: what problem does elastic reserve solve vs existing reserved pools? short bullets pls.
jamie: short: customers with committed capacity need predictable baseline but occasionally want bursts without buying bigger commit. current reserved pools + hard quotas block UX — they either buy bigger or hit rejects. elastic approach = baseline reserved + small shared burst buffer (soft tokens) that can be reclaimed.
ash: sounds reasonable. can you sketch ops constraints? reclaim rules, preempt severity, and perf SLOs when reclaimed.
jamie: ops notes in-thread: reclaim rule = LRU across tenants in same billing tier; soft tokens reclaimed under 95% cluster capacity for >30s. preempt severity = graceful drain (10s notify via signal), migrate long-running jobs to lower tier or queue. SLO when reclaimed = best-effort, target p50 latency increase <20% for affected requests.
lucy: do we allow cross-region bursting? some EMEA customers asked for global spillover.
jamie: prefer no cross-region by default for data locality. add opt-in flag per tenant to allow cross-region spillover (audit & egress cost notes).
kevin: what's the config surface for customers? example plz.
jamie: example config snippet:
```
reserved_capacity: 200vCPU-equivalent
burst_buffer: 50 (soft tokens)
burst_policy:
  reclaim: lru
  preempt_grace_s: 10
  recovery_window_s: 120
  cross_region_spill: false
```
kevin: good. launch criteria? what must be in place before GA?
jamie: proposed launch criteria (MUST):
- deterministic accounting for soft token usage per-tenant (billing + audit)
- reclaim + preempt hooks implemented in runtime
- rollout circuit breaker (can disable soft buffer per cluster)
- e2e perf test showing <5% cost regression vs baseline at 80% utilization
- docs + console UI for buffer size and usage visualization
ash: add: policy simulator for QA so we can run policy against synthetic workloads and estimate tenant impact.
jamie: added. also acceptance criteria for customers: 2 pilot customers (one infra-heavy, one latency-sensitive) on Dedicated with soft buffer enabled and follow-up regression report.
lucy: risk list?
jamie: major risks: billing disputes (need clear visibility), noisy neighbor effect if reclaim policy not strict, complexity in capacity planning for SRE. mitigations: per-tenant dashboards, emergency kill switch, telemetry to detect abuse.
kevin: prioritization ask: where does this land against autoscale improvements and dedicated preemption work?
jamie: propose sequencing: 1) policy primitives + accounting (Q2), 2) runtime preempt hooks + graceful drain (Q3), 3) console + pilot + simulator (Q4). tie to dedicated autoscale by sharing reclaim signals; this is complementary not blocker.
ash: scope negotiation: can we ship a v1 without cross-region spill? yes. can we limit initial pilots to nodes with homogeneous hardware? yes.
lucy: customer-driven asks: X-Plat requested larger burst windows (5m) and per-route caps. can we support configurable recovery_window_s and per-route soft caps?
jamie: yes, we'll expose those as advanced flags for pilots. default recovery_window_s = 120s, but configurable up to 5m with warning in UI.
ops-bot: deploy-plan reminder: Please add feature flag `soft_burst_v1` and schedule canary on staging clusters before Q3 rollout.
kevin: next steps: jamie to draft spec doc with the config schema + rehearsal plan, ash to prototype simulator, lucy to line up pilot customers. aim to have spec ready by EOD Friday.
jamie: will do. tagging follow-ups: @kevin @ash @lucy. thumbs up if ok :thumbsup:
kevin: :thumbsup:
ash: :thumbsup:
lucy: :+1:
